thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High error rate — serving-runtime-prod. Metric: 5xx spikes tied to GPU node gpu-12. Recent container crashes with CUDA illegal memory access / misaligned address observed. Dashboard: https://rwd.internal/dash/alerts/1801505678

laura-oncall: ack — paging. I'm on it, switching to this incident thread. Running quick checks now.

laura-oncall: kubectl get pods -n inference | grep gpu-12

sam-eng: i'm on node gpu-12. dmesg shows repeated 'misaligned address' followed by GPU illegal memory access. Containers on that node are crashlooping.

sam-eng: dmesg excerpt:
```
[ 12345.678901] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:05:00): 31, Ch 00000000, ...
[ 12345.679001] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:05:00): 31, pid=2712, ...
[ 12345.679101] kernel: nv_crash: illegal memory access at 0x00000000
```

jake-sre: plan: isolate node -> taint & drain, fail traffic to smaller model-variant, rollback recent batching config if it correlates. Preparing commands.

jake-sre: kubectl taint nodes gpu-12 node.kubernetes.io/unavailable=maintenance:NoSchedule
kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force

deploy-bot: deploy: routing update initiated by deploy-bot: /v1/generate -> model:gpt-small-v1 (canary -> 100%) at 2026-03-15T18:03:40Z

maya-ml: FYI — we pushed a batching config change ~30m ago that bumped max_batch_size from 8 -> 16 on the /v1/generate route. That would increase GPU mem pressure for long sequences.

laura-oncall: noted. rolling back batching.max_batch_size -> 8 now.

deploy-bot: config rollback: batching.max_batch_size set to 8 for route /v1/generate (rev 2026-03-15T17:35Z) — success

rachel-cse: customer impact? Which API keys/customers seeing errors? We should prepare a status update and notify affected accounts.

laura-oncall: current telemetry: 12 unique API keys produced 5xx within last 10m. Two enterprise customers (acme-inc, finserve) show sustained elevated error rates. Drafting status page and notifying AMs.

jake-sre: mitigation status: after taint/drain + route change, 5xx rate dropped close to baseline. Continue to monitor for 20m before declaring containment.

sam-eng: captured a CUDA stack dump from one of the crashed containers — possible OOB memory access in custom kernel/cudnn call:
```
#0  0x7f9e4a1b in cuLaunchKernel ...
#1  0x7f9e5c2d in cudnnConvolutionForward ...
#2  0x5566ab7 in inference::Runner::runBatch ...
```

maya-ml: hypothesizing root cause: race in KV cache eviction + increased batch size causing out-of-bounds index in our custom kernel. Also possible alignment issue when using quantized tensors on this cudnn release. Need repro.

laura-oncall: immediate action items:
- sam-eng: collect full dmesg, container stdout/stderr, and GPU coredump. Upload to s3://redwood-incidents/1801505678/ with perms = private.
- jake-sre: draft incident page, severity triage, coordinate postmortem owners.
- maya-ml: attempt minimal repro on dev GPU with batching.max_batch_size=16 and long sequences.
- rachel-cse: open support tickets for acme-inc and finserve, prep customer-facing note.

laura-oncall: handing off to @jake in 10m for continuing coordination — I have an EMER call. Keep me tagged for any regression.

jake-sre: taking over. I'll keep this thread as the timeline. Scheduling 1h postmortem with owners.

incident-bot: Incident Sev2 acknowledged by jake-sre. Notifications sent to eng-leads, product, and legal. Incident timeline channel created: #incidents/1801505678.

laura-oncall: :white_check_mark: last note before handoff — error rate back to baseline, drained node rebalanced, routing fallback holding. If anything regresses, @jake will page.
